title: The voice: how we speak
examples: Teacher, what exactly are vocal cords?
How does my tongue help me talk?

explain.say: Today we learn how we make the sounds we use to talk.
Your vocal cords are two small bands inside your voice box.
When you breathe out, air travels up from your lungs.
The air makes your vocal cords vibrate when you speak.

items: Vibration: Cords shake back and forth

explain.say: Your tongue and lips shape the sound into words we understand.
When you say the word 'tea', your tongue moves and your lips form the shape.

faq.q: Do I need to breathe first to talk?
faq.a: Yes, you need air from your lungs to start the sound. The air pushes the vocal cords to make them vibrate.
asks: Do I need breath to speak?

faq.q: What are the vocal cords made of?
faq.a: They are bands of tissue located inside your larynx. They are what vibrate when air passes over them.
asks: What is in my voice box?
What material are the vocal cords?

faq.q: How do my lips change the sound?
faq.a: Your lips help you make sounds by closing them or rounding them. This changes the shape of the sound coming out.
asks: Do my lips help me talk?
How do I make an 'o' sound?

faq.q: Is talking the same as singing?
faq.a: Both use your vocal cords and air, but singing often uses more controlled vibration. Talking uses specific shapes from your tongue and lips.
asks: Do I use my tongue differently when singing?

faq.a: You might lose your voice if your vocal cords become swollen or irritated. Resting your voice helps them heal.
asks: Why does my voice get hoarse?

facts: The vocal cords are located inside the larynx, or voice box.
Sound is created when air causes the vocal cords to vibrate.
The tongue and lips change the sound into specific words.
Breathing provides the necessary air pressure for speech.

quiz.say: Which body part vibrates to create sound?
quiz.why: The vocal cords are the specific bands of tissue that vibrate when air passes over them to make sound.

wrong.1: The lungs provide the air, but they do not vibrate themselves to make the sound.
wrong.2: The tongue shapes the sound, but it is not the main vibrating source.
wrong.3: The lips help shape the sound, but they do not create the initial vibration.

quiz.say: What is the main source of power for speech?
quiz.why: Air from the lungs provides the necessary force or pressure to make the vocal cords vibrate.

wrong.0: The vocal cords vibrate, but they need air pressure from the lungs to vibrate strongly.
wrong.1: Opening the lips only helps to release the sound, it does not power it.
wrong.3: The tongue muscles help shape the sound, but they do not provide the air power.

quiz.say: If I want to say the word 'see', which parts work together?

options.show: only the air from the lungs
options.say: only the air from the lungs

quiz.why: You need the air from the lungs to vibrate the vocal cords, and then the tongue and lips shape that vibration into the specific sound 'see'.

wrong.0: Without air from the lungs, the vocal cords cannot vibrate to make any sound at all.
wrong.1: Just air blowing out makes noise, but the vocal cords and tongue are needed to make it a word.
wrong.3: The vocal cords need air to vibrate, and they also need the tongue and lips to shape the sound.
